headline: From Loss to Leadership: How One Amputee Built Hope for Thousands
meta_description: Valeria Adzo Adzatia lost her limb at age 7. Now her foundation supports over 1,000 amputees in Ghana through counselling, rehabilitation, and peer mentorship.
summary_short: A Ghanaian woman who became an amputee as a child founded Smiles of Hope, helping thousands rebuild their lives through counselling and community support.
body:
Valeria Adzo Adzatia lost a limb at age 7, but transformed that personal tragedy into a mission that has reached thousands of amputees across Ghana. Through the Smiles of Hope Foundation, she offers counselling, rehabilitation, and peer mentorship to help beneficiaries regain confidence and reintegrate into society.

Recognized for her impact this year, Adzatia dedicated the award to amputees across Ghana and her team, framing their collective work as a message of hope. Her foundation has supported more than 1,000 amputees—each journey marked by the belief that no one should walk that path alone. By combining professional support with the lived experience of her peers, Smiles of Hope has created a network where people facing similar struggles find both practical tools and human connection.
quick_facts: Valeria Adzo Adzatia lost a limb at age 7
Smiles of Hope Foundation has reached over 1,000 amputees in Ghana
Services include counselling, rehabilitation, and peer mentorship
Focus on rebuilding confidence and reintegrating into society
